name: Loba
description: Loba (Spanish for 'She-Wolf') is a popular Rummy-style card game widely played in Argentina, Bolivia, Uruguay, and across South America. Similar to Continental Rummy and Carioca, it is played over multiple rounds with increasing difficulty. Players aim to form specific combinations of 'Juegos' (Sets) and 'Escaleras' (Sequences). It is known for its fast pace and the inclusion of Jokers as powerful wildcards.

history.origins: Believed to have evolved from the Spanish game 'ChinchÃ³n' and the broader European 'Continental Rummy' family in the mid-20th century. The name 'Loba' evokes the 'wolfish' nature of stealing opponents' discards and the predatory approach to collecting cards.
timeline: 1940s: Rummy variants spread through the Rio de la Plata region of South America.
1960s: 'Loba' becomes a favorite social game for clubs and families in Buenos Aires and Montevideo.
1980s: Regional variations solidify; Loba de Mar (Sea Wolf) variant popularized in coastal regions.
Present: One of the most common card games in Argentine and Uruguayan household culture, often played at summer resorts and family gatherings.
2010s: Digital versions gain popularity on mobile platforms across Latin America.
history.cultural: Commonly played as 'Loba de Mar' (Sea Wolf) in coastal regions of Argentina and Uruguay. The game is a staple of South American social card gaming, bridging generations at family gatherings.
history.evolution: The game's scoring system, where high-value cards like Jokers carry massive penalties, was designed to discourage 'holding' high cards to the end of a round. The multi-round structure with escalating contracts adds strategic depth.

setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 11 cards (in some variants 13). The remaining cards form the stock pile. One card is turned up to start the discard pile.

rules.objective: Form all cards in your hand into valid melds and 'go out' (empty your hand). Lowest cumulative score across all rounds wins.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Draw**: On your turn, draw one card from the stock or take the top card from the discard pile. 2. **Melding**: You can lay down melds as soon as you have them. In the first round, you usually need a minimum 'opening' count (e.g., 30 or 40 points in some variants). 3. **Laying Off**: You can add cards to your own or opponents' existing melds on the table. 4. **Discard**: End your turn by discarding one card to the discard pile.
keyRules: Juego (Set): 3+ cards of same rank (different suits).
Escalera (Sequence): 3+ consecutive cards of same suit.
Jokers and sometimes 2s act as wildcards.
Sequence cannot consist solely of wildcards.
Must draw before melding or laying off.
Must end turn with a discard (unless going out).
Can lay off on opponents' melds once you've opened.
Going out ends the round; remaining cards count as penalties.

strategy.basic: Keep your Jokers! They are your best chance to complete a long sequence. However, if you see an opponent has only 2 cards left, discard your Joker immediately to avoid the 50-point penalty. Prioritize forming sequences over setsâ€”they're harder for opponents to block.
strategy.intermediate: Opening Strategy: Don't 'open' (lay down cards) as soon as you hit the minimum if you have cards that could be easily played off by others. Wait until you can lay down most of your hand at once. Watch the discard pileâ€”if the player to your left keeps taking your discards, stop feeding them cards they need.
strategy.advanced: Discard Control: Pay attention to what the person to your left is picking up from the discard pile. If they pick up a 7 of Spades, they are likely building a 'Seven' set or a Spades sequenceâ€”do not feed them Spades! The 'Loba' play: Sometimes hold a complete meld in hand to surprise opponents, going out unexpectedly when they think they have time.
tips: Prioritize 'Escaleras' (Sequences) over 'Juegos' (Sets). Sequences are easier to extend and yield more opportunities to 'lay off' cards later.
In Loba, the 2 is often a 'clean' cardâ€”use it naturally in sequences rather than as a wildcard unless desperate.
Watch opponents' card counts. When someone is down to 2-3 cards, be very careful about what you discard.
If you have multiple possible melds, lay down the one that gives you the most flexibility for laying off remaining cards.

scoring.description: Penalty points for cards remaining in hand when another player goes out.
scoring.winCondition: Lowest cumulative score after agreed number of rounds or when a player reaches a penalty threshold (e.g., 200 points).
